subject: Hosting constraints, runbook, and pilot timetable
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Park <epark@clarityhealth.ai>, Clarity Health Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosting constraints, runbook, and pilot timetable

Hi Elena / Clarity team — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared playbook for the PoC: 

1) Key constraints you raised
- PHI / HIPAA scope: production data must remain in your VPC / on-prem for auditability.
- Procurement: a standard PO + security questionnaire is required before prod access.
- Timeline preference: pilot (sandbox) as soon as late Nov, production decision by end of Q1.

2) Recommended two-track PoC sequence (what we propose)
A. Sandbox (low risk) — Hosted API for feature validation (2 weeks)
  - Purpose: verify integration, prompts, embeddings, and basic latency/quality.
  - Owner: Laura (sales) + Clarity dev lead.
B. Performance & compliance track — Dedicated capacity + Private VPC evaluation (3–5 weeks)
  - Purpose: throughput & latency benchmarking, data residency / KMS evaluation, SOC2 evidence.
  - Owner: Marcus (solutions) + Clarity infra/security.

3) Success criteria (suggested; please edit)
- Functional: API integration complete, basic flows working end-to-end.
- Latency: 95th percentile < 220ms for prompt sizes up to 1k tokens (dedicated).
- Throughput: sustained 12 reqs/sec on a dedicated 4-GPU pool for the primary endpoint.
- Security: evidence of KMS integration and network controls in the private trial.

4) Immediate asks from Redwood
- Confirm whether Clarity will allow a short (non-PHI) dataset for the hosted sandbox test.
- Share the procurement contact and expected PO cadence.
- Provide a point of contact for infra/security for the dedicated/private setup.

Attachments: clarity_poc_requirements.xlsx (your worksheet), redwood_pilot_runbook.pdf (runbook draft)

If that looks good I can propose concrete dates for the week of Nov 29 for kickoff of the sandbox track and schedule a separate infra sync for the following week.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Dr. Elena Park <epark@clarityhealth.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Clarity Health Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting constraints, runbook, and pilot timetable

Thanks for the clear recap, Grace — and to the team for taking notes. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Production requirement: yes, PHI must remain in our VPC. We cannot send PHI to hosted endpoints unless it goes through a tokenization/obfuscation step we control.
- Sandbox: we can provide a synthetic dataset (non-PHI) for an initial Hosted API validation. That's what I'd like to see first.
- Dedicated vs Private: preference is to evaluate Dedicated capacity for performance benchmarking, then move to Private VPC for production if results are positive and procurement clears. In short: Hosted sandbox -> Dedicated perf -> Private for prod.
- Procurement: cc'd procurement (procurement@clarityhealth.ai). We work with annual master services agreements; likely process is MSAs + SOW + PO. Expect a 4–6 week procurement lead time once terms are agreed.

Questions for Redwood: 
1) Can you confirm Redwood's standard MSA and whether we will need any additional Business Associate Addendum (BAA) for HIPAA?
2) For the Dedicated benchmark, what instance types / GPU profiles should we expect?
3) Any SOC2 / penetration test reports we can review before the infra sync?

Appreciate the runbook and the workbook. I will share the procurement calendar and a security point-of-contact by EOD.

Best,
Elena

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Dr. Elena Park <epark@clarityhealth.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Clarity Health Procurement <procurement@clarityhealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosting constraints, runbook, and pilot timetable

Elena — thanks for the quick clarifications. A few technical notes and a proposed schedule from the solutions side so you can share with your infra/security partner: 

Technical plan (high level)
- Sandbox (Hosted API): no PHI, quick integration, we can spin keys and an environment within 24 hours once accounts are provisioned. Good for verifying prompts, embeddings and SDK usage.
- Dedicated benchmark: we propose a 3-week window to run repeatable throughput and latency tests. We'll provide Docker images, a standard load-generator harness, and a benchmark script (open-sourced).
- Private VPC: for prod we will deploy a Private control plane with egress/nat rules defined by your network team. We integrate with customer KMS (you keep keys).

Preliminary performance targets (for planning)
- P95 latency target: <=220ms (short prompts, warm cache) on a 4xA100-style pool.
- Steady-state throughput: 10–15 rps sustained for our sample workload.
- Token cost: we'll run a cost estimate during the benchmark window and share a token-level breakdown.

Security/compliance deliverables we can attach before the infra sync:
- SOC2 Type II summary (redacted where needed).
- Pen test summary and remediation plan.
- BAA template and guidance on where to insert any additional clauses for PHI handling.

Proposed timeline (concrete)
- Week of Nov 29: Hosted sandbox kickoff (2 weeks).
- Week of Dec 13: Dedicated benchmark kickoff (3 weeks).
- Early Jan: Private VPC planning + procurement handoff.

Next steps from Redwood (what we'll do)
- Share a cleaned runbook (redwood_pilot_runbook.pdf) with step-by-step infra tasks for your network team.
- Send SOC2 summary + pen-test docs to procurement and security.
- Provide a proposed Dedicated configuration (GPU counts and expected costs) in a follow-up email by EOD tomorrow.

Attachment note: I've attached an internal benchmark template to the runbook PDF; happy to tailor it.

-- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
